status: frozen before empirical fitting; all numeric constants are provisional and uncalibrated (no real-paper calibration exists; synthetic checks only)
data_regime: same-data reconstruction from author-processed deposit aggregates

implementation_agreement.rule: Two implementations agree on a grid row when both have status ok, equal n_obs, equal sample_hash, |estimate difference| <= max(1e-8, 0.001 x mean benchmark SE) and benchmark SEs within 0.5% of each other. Descriptive outputs agree when every reported statistic is within relative 1e-6 or absolute 1e-9.
implementation_agreement.justification: Same data and fully specified definitions leave only floating-point and solver differences; 0.001 SE is far below any substantive band.
implementation_agreement.claim_use: A claim is scored on an agreeing pair at its origin row (A-B, A-C or B-C, in that order of preference); the third implementation, if it disagrees, goes to code audit. With no agreeing pair the claim is indeterminate: implementation_disagreement. Agreement and dispersion across the full grid are reported separately.

rounding: A printed number with d decimals is the interval [v - 0.5 x 10^-d, v + 0.5 x 10^-d]. All comparisons use the whole interval.
sign: Assessed only when the published rounding interval excludes zero. Agreement means the reconstructed estimate is nonzero with the published sign.

magnitude.measure: z = distance from the reconstructed estimate to the published rounding interval (0 inside), divided by the printed published SE
magnitude.also_reported: relative difference estimate / published - 1 and absolute difference
magnitude.justification: Same-data regime: exact reproduction is the expectation, so half an SE is a tight match band; beyond 2 SE the published 95% interval would not contain the reconstruction.

inference.published_band: from printed stars using the Table 3 legend (*** < .01, ** < .05, * < .10, none >= .10), applied to every table with stars

benchmark.panel_linear: CR1 cluster-robust by county (assignment unit), t with G-1 df
benchmark.few_cluster_rule: below 30 clusters: wild cluster bootstrap with Rademacher weights and restricted residuals; no in-scope model is expected to fall below it
benchmark.threshold_justification: provisional, from the cluster-robust inference literature (Cameron, Gelbach and Miller 2008; MacKinnon and Webb 2017)

inference.native: Table 4, Table 5 Panel B and Figure 5 state HC robust errors (native = HC1); Figure 4 states county clustering (native = CR1). Tables 3, 5A, 6 and 7 do not state the method: native unknown, both HC1 and CR1 are reported.
inference.band_change: difference in band index, positive = weaker than published. A positive significance claim is not failed by stronger significance. For a published nonsignificant estimate, a reconstruction with p < .05 is a two-band contradiction.

n_obs.use: N mismatch prevents a consistent outcome and gives indeterminate: sample_reconstruction, or indeterminate: inconsistent_targets where a forensic record shows the printed N is internally inconsistent

regression_claim_outcome.consistent: origin: sign agrees (or not assessable), magnitude match, benchmark band equal to or stronger than published, N match or near
regression_claim_outcome.fragile_inference: origin: sign agrees and magnitude match, but the benchmark band is weaker than published by one band or more while the HC1 band (or native band where stated) is not weaker
regression_claim_outcome.discrepant_candidate: origin fails at least one of: sign opposite; benchmark band weaker by two or more bands (or two-band contradiction of nonsignificance); magnitude mismatch. AND no uncertain-branch row for the claim passes all of sign agreement, band within one, magnitude z <= 2.0. Becomes discrepant only after adversarial review; otherwise indeterminate with the review's reason.
regression_claim_outcome.indeterminate: everything else, with sub-codes: magnitude_grey_zone, label_sensitive (origin fails but an uncertain branch passes), sample_reconstruction, inconsistent_targets, unavailable_criterion, failed_fit
regression_claim_outcome.specification_fragility: No genuinely equivalent alternatives exist in the frozen grid (all alternatives are uncertain or non-equivalent), so specification fragility is not assessed for any claim.
regression_claim_outcome.label_sensitivity_report: For each claim, the share of uncertain-branch rows that keep the published sign and benchmark p < .05, the median and range of estimates, and the published estimate's position. If treating uncertain rows as equivalent would yield fragile (share < 0.8 for a claim published significant at .05), the claim is flagged label_sensitive and both readings are reported.

special_claims.placebo: Table 5 Panel A columns 3-4. Sign and magnitude are not audited (the draw differs). Consistent if the benchmark p >= .10; a benchmark p < .05 is a two-band contradiction. The 200-draw distribution (share with p < .05 and quantiles) is reported.
special_claims.distance_nuisance: Table 6 Distance rows. Magnitude is compared under kilometres (origin) and miles (coefficient x 1.609344); the unit is unstated, so a match under either is consistent and a mismatch under both is assessed as usual.

descriptive_claims.table1: Per row: treated mean, control mean, difference compared by relative deviation r = distance to rounding interval / |published|; match r = 0, near r <= 0.01, moderate r <= 0.10, mismatch r > 0.10. Printed p compared by band. Row consistent if all three values are match or near and p in the same band; discrepant_candidate if a mean is mismatch at the origin and under every uncertain reading of the row's variable; otherwise indeterminate: measurement.
descriptive_claims.table2: Per row: mean and median compared as above; SD, min and max reported. Row consistent if mean and median are match or near; discrepant_candidate if the mean is mismatch at origin and every uncertain reading; otherwise indeterminate: measurement.
descriptive_claims.counts: Figures 1-2 county counts: exact match consistent; within 1% indeterminate: near; otherwise discrepant_candidate.

plot_points.point_rule: A reconstructed point matches a reading when it lies within the reading interval widened on each side by half its width; with two readers the union of their widened intervals is used.
plot_points.series_outcome: consistent if at least 80% of read points match; otherwise indeterminate: plot_reading. Plot readings never yield a discrepant outcome.

paper_level.basis: The abstract and introduction state the main findings as lower follow-on contributions and contributor activity (difference-in-differences and cross-sectional) and lower long-term quality (D01 p.1-2). Both readers tier these focal; total contributions (T3/T4 columns 1-2) and the Table 7 mechanism tests stay focal at claim level but are not paper-focal.
paper_level.rule: 1) If any paper-focal claim is indeterminate or not attemptable, the paper is indeterminate (scoring instructions). 2) Else if at least half of the paper-focal claims are discrepant after review, not reproduced. 3) Else if any paper-focal claim is discrepant or fragile, or any other tier has a discrepant claim, partially reproduced. 4) Else if all paper-focal claims are consistent, fully reproduced. Fragile-inference focal claims with the rest consistent are reported as 'consistent with fragile inference' and not mapped.
paper_level.justification: Avoids a worst-cell rule across nine focal estimates while keeping the instruction that indeterminate focal evidence makes the paper indeterminate.

alpha: 0.05 two-sided (D01 p.12 'not statistically significant at the 95% level'); hypothesized direction negative for activity outcomes and positive for the error score
budget: grid: one full run per implementation, at most 6 hours wall each; influence: implementation A for all deletions, implementation C for a fixed 50-county subset per model; failures retained
calibration: uncalibrated; no planted-error, null-data or post-cutoff arms were run beyond synthetic recovery checks of the implementations
